title: SDK: First 12 Hours — Accelerator Lab Notes
content:
Purpose:
- Fast, time-boxed lab to take a new engineer from zero to a minimal production-like SDK integration within 12 hours.
- Emphasis: high signal, low friction, repeatable for workshops and customer POCs.
- This doc = working notes + checklist + TODOs for the accelerator kit.

Audience:
- New hires (engineer/ML engineer), partner integration engineers, Solutions Engineers running half-day POCs.

Success criteria (end of 12h):
- App can call Redwood API with auth + fallbacks and handle streaming responses without blocking the UI.
- Basic telemetry visible in Console: per-route latency, token counts, at least one error captured and traced.
- Cost guardrail: request-level estimated token cost shown; can simulate a cap.
- Local dev run that mocks a simple KV cache and demonstrates prefix-caching behavior.

High-level flow (time-boxed):
- 0:00–0:30 — Setup: repo clone, creds, quick env sanity (curl + SDK ping).
  - readme-check: minimal steps to get a token and run `./dev/hello.sh`
  - smoke commands: curl /v1/models -> expect JSON + model list; SDK ping -> "ok"
- 0:30–1:30 — Minimal generation: REST call -> streamed tokens -> render in web console.
  - sample prompt: "summarize this paragraph in one sentence"
  - show fallback toggle: switch to cheaper model (quantized) and compare latency/cost
- 1:30–3:00 — Embedder + Retrieval stub: create embedding, index 10 docs locally, rerank -> show top-3 recall change.
- 3:00–5:00 — Error modes + resilience: forced rate limit, 500s, long-tail latency; test automatic retry, circuit-breaker, and fallback to cached response.
- 5:00–7:00 — Instrumentation: add token counters, attach trace id to request, propagate into logs and Console.
- 7:00–9:00 — Model rollouts: configure a canary route (10% traffic) -> observe metrics and do manual rollback.
- 9:00–11:00 — Cost/perf tuning: enable batching (simulate 100 concurrent requests locally with load tool), enable KV prefix caching; measure tokens/unit.
- 11:00–12:00 — Wrap-up: checklist, capture screenshots, record common failure notes for next cohort.

Lab components (what accelerator repo should include):
- quickstart/README.md with 6 commands (clone, env, install, run dev server, smoke, teardown).
- samples/streaming-demo: minimal React page that mounts a stream and shows partial tokens as they arrive.
- samples/embed-rerank: JS script + small dataset, step-by-step comments, expected outputs in /expected.
- infra/dev-sim: lightweight script to simulate rate limits and high-latency nodes (env flag to toggle).
- telemetry/hooks: example middleware injecting trace id + token-meter; small Grafana/Console dashboard json with required charts.
- ops/policies.yaml: brief examples for canary rollout and fallback mapping (model -> quantized-model).

Developer notes / common pitfalls (raw):
- Credentials: most friction still when a user misplaces token scope. Add `redwood token inspect` helper.
- Streaming: devs often forget to flush on partial token writes -> UI stalls; provide client helper that writes incremental chunks.
- Batching + dev mode: local dev typically disables batching which hides batching regressions; include an opt-in sim that combines concurrent requests.
- Embedding dimensionality: default model has 1536 dims; some Naive index libs choke on 0-based indexes — include prebuilt index file for the lab.
- Rollouts: ensure the route config returns metadata (variant id) so developers can tell which model served request.

Quick checklists (copyable):
- Pre-lab host checklist:
  - [ ] Account with API token created and scoped
  - [ ] Browser with local dev certs (if running secure websocket streaming)
  - [ ] Node >= 18 or Python 3.10 installed
  - [ ] Docker (optional) for dev-sim scripts
- Post-lab handoff checklist:
  - [ ] Screenshots: streaming UI + console traces + per-route chart
  - [ ] Capture: one failing scenario + steps to reproduce
  - [ ] Add notes to cohort tracker (spreadsheet link in linked_artifacts)

Teaching tips for instructor running the lab:
- Start by demoing the streaming UI for 2 minutes to hook audience.
- Use the rate-limit failure intentionally; students react more to fixing a break than to a happy-path.
- Encourage toggling the model variant; talk about the cost/perf tradeoff aloud with numbers.
- Pair people into teams of two during the embedding/rerank section.

Telemetry & gating (minimal required signals):
- Request count (per-route), median latency(50/95), token count per request, error rate per model variant, fallback count.
- Gated metric for lab: after enabling canary, 95th latency must not increase >20% over baseline or automatic rollback triggers.

Open questions / TODOs (priority ordered):
- [P0] Make `dev/hello.sh` also validate that streaming works through corporate proxy (some enterprises block WS).
- [P0] Add a tiny mock for KV prefix caching that shows saved hit/miss counters in UI.
- [P1] Create small classroom exercises (5–10 minute prompts) for each time slice so instructors can timebox easily.
- [P2] Pre-generate a failing trace with a deterministic flaky node for reproducible debugging practice.
- [P3] Author a short "How we measure token cost" sidebar for the README so customers understand accounting.

Appendix: handy commands & snippets
- Smoke token inspect: `REDWOOD_TOKEN=xxx node ./scripts/inspect-token.js`
- Streaming sample (curl): `curl -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate?stream=true -d \"{\"prompt\":\"hey\"}\"`
- Quick batch sim (node): `node infra/load-sim.js --concurrency 100 --route /api/generate`

Notes to self:
- Keep lab under 500MB -> no heavyweight data or full embeddings index.
- Make sure the Console dashboard import is 1-click (file in telemetry/hooks/dashboard.json).
- Schedule pilot internal run with Solutions Eng on 2025-11-18.

End of doc.

(Informal; will extract into README + instructor guide once pilot feedback collected.)
